title: Bind the named-project scope token to local resolution or a not-resolvable error
description:
Extend the addressing core's scope parsing so a `@<project>` address distinguishes the local project (which resolves) from any other named project (which is syntactically valid but not resolvable locally), per this epic's REQ-09 and this story's design decision D5. This item adds no path parsing of its own and builds no federation or remote lookup — only the local-vs-other binding.

Today `Scope` (crates/jit/src/domain/item.rs:89-152) has exactly two variants, `Scope::Issue(String)` and `Scope::Project`, and `Scope::parse` (item.rs:113-119) treats a bare `@` as `Scope::Project` and every other string as an issue short-id verbatim — it has no notion of a project NAME at all. A repo-wide search shows `Scope::parse` is currently called only from item.rs's own doctests and unit tests; no production call site exists yet (the kind-segmented address parser/resolver that will eventually call this lives in a separate, sibling story of this epic).

What to build, in `crates/jit/src/domain/item.rs`:
- Add a third `Scope` variant representing a reference to a project other than the local one, e.g. `Scope::OtherProject(String)`, carrying the referenced project name verbatim.
- Extend the parsing entry point (either by adding a local-project-name parameter to `Scope::parse` itself, or a sibling pure function, at item.rs:113-119) so that, given the declared local project name as a plain `&str` input (the caller supplies the already-loaded config value — this keeps the function pure domain code with no file I/O, per this project's layering rule that domain logic must be free of I/O):
  - segment `"@"` -> `Scope::Project` (unchanged from today).
  - segment `"@<name>"` where `<name>` equals the supplied local project name -> `Scope::Project`.
  - segment `"@<name>"` where `<name>` differs from the supplied local project name -> `Scope::OtherProject(name)`.
  - No case returns an `Err` from parsing itself — every `@`-prefixed segment is syntactically valid. The `@`-vs-other structural check must be the same one `Scope::parse` already performs, not a re-implemented ad hoc string match.
- Add a new `ItemError` variant (crates/jit/src/domain/item.rs:245-355 shows the existing `thiserror` enum pattern to follow), e.g. `ItemError::NotResolvable { project: String }`, with a `#[error(...)]` message that names the unresolvable project and states plainly that no federation or remote lookup was attempted.
- Add a resolution-facing function (or method on `Scope`) that, given a `Scope::OtherProject(name)`, returns `Err(ItemError::NotResolvable { project: name })`; given `Scope::Project` or `Scope::Issue`, returns the existing successful path. This is the "returns a clear not-resolvable error" behavior the story requires, exercised at the domain layer since no consuming CLI command exists yet in this codebase.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: unit tests in `domain/item.rs` prove that, given a supplied local project name (e.g. `"acme"`), both `"@"` and `"@acme"` parse to `Scope::Project`, and that the same structural `@`-prefix check used by the existing `Scope::parse` is reused (no duplicate ad hoc string-matching function).
- [hard] REQ-02: a unit test proves `"@other-project"` (local name `"acme"`) parses without error into `Scope::OtherProject("other-project".to_string())`, distinct from `Scope::Project` and `Scope::Issue`; a second unit test proves the resolution-facing function returns `Err(ItemError::NotResolvable { project })` for that value, with a `to_string()` message that contains `"other-project"` and contains no mention of any network/remote attempt (the message states resolution is local-only).
